cases.name: migrate
cases.promptMarkdown:
This solution is moving to .NET 11.
Its test project already targets net10.0 and net11.0, and global.json uses the .NET 11 SDK.
Make the code behave correctly on .NET 11, keep the results the tests describe, and change only what needs to change.
Build and test with `./test.sh`, which runs both frameworks and writes TestResults/summary.txt.
Use `./dotnet` instead of `dotnet` for any other SDK command; it keeps the SDK's files inside this folder.
Do not change the tests.
When you are done, list every conversion or rounding you looked at and what you did with it.

graders.name: report
graders.evidence:
`./test.sh` now passes all 30 tests on both net10.0 and net11.0, and the build reports 0 DCV warnings. The tests are unchanged. Before the fix, net11.0 failed 16 tests and net10.0 failed 1. The sandbox denied some network requests (nuget.org and builds.dotnet.microsoft.com), but the build and tests ran anyway.

I added one helper file, `src/Desk.Core/FloatingPoint.cs`, with `ToDecimal(double)` and `Normalize(decimal)`. The analyzer package was already referenced, so it stays. Each site I kept has a `#pragma warning disable` with its reason, which accounts for the 7 suppressions the summary counts.

## Changed sites (11 sites in 8 files)

| File | Warning | Expression | Source → sink | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Fees/FeeSchedule.cs` | DCV002 | `(decimal)0.0004` | constant | Wrote the literal `0.0004m`. This was the one net10.0 failure. |
| `Fees/FeeSchedule.cs` | DCV005 | `(decimal)Math.Round((double)amount, 2)` | decimal sent through a double | Now `FloatingPoint.Normalize(Math.Round(amount, 2))`. `Normalize` keeps the old text form, so 1.2 doesn't print as 1.20. |
| `Invoices/LineTotal.cs` | DCV004 | `Math.Round(amount, 2, AwayFromZero)` | written amount → nearest round that can land on a midpoint | Now `(double)decimal.Round(ToDecimal(amount), 2, AwayFromZero)`. 655.925 gives 655.93 again. |
| `Orders/LotSizer.cs` | DCV001 | `(decimal)requested` | written size → floor to a lot step | `ToDecimal` |
| `Orders/OrderText.cs` | DCV001 ×2 | `(decimal)qty`, `(decimal)price` | written values → default `ToString` in order text | `ToDecimal` on both, so the text carries no 28-digit tail. |
| `Pricing/PriceRounding.cs` | DCV003 ×2 | `Math.Round(price, decimals, ToNegativeInfinity / ToPositiveInfinity)` | written price → directed rounding | `(double)decimal.Round(ToDecimal(price), decimals, mode)` in both `Bid` and `Ask`. |
| `Pricing/TickInfo.cs` | DCV001 | `(decimal)tickSize` | written tick size → `Scale` | `ToDecimal` |
| `Reports/PnlReport.cs` | DCV001 | `(decimal)(price * qty)` | product of written values → nearest round to cents | `ToDecimal`. The 2.675 × 1.0 test case needs this to give 2.68. |
| `Risk/BalanceCheck.cs` | DCV001 | `(decimal)available` | written balance → `>=` comparison | `ToDecimal` |

## Kept sites (suppressed with a reason)

| File | Warning | Expression | Why it stays |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Analytics/FillStats.cs` | DCV001 | `(decimal)(filled / requested)` | A computed ratio, rounded to nearest at one decimal. |
| `Analytics/Volatility.cs` | DCV001 | `(decimal)(stdDev * Math.Sqrt(365))` | A computed volatility, rounded to nearest at four decimals. |
| `Analytics/Ranking.cs` | DCV001 | `(decimal)s.Value` | Used for ordering only. |
| `Diagnostics/LatencyLog.cs` | DCV001 | `(decimal)ms` with `:F2` | Fixed-format display of a measurement. |
| `Time/Buckets.cs` | DCV001 | `(decimal)Math.Floor(seconds / 60)` | An integral value below 1e15, so the extra digits can't show. |
| `Pricing/MidPrice.cs` | DCV004 | `Math.Round((bid + ask) / 2, 8)` in `Mid` | A computed value. Keeping `Math.Round` also avoids the decimal route throwing on NaN, infinity or out-of-range values. |
| `Pricing/MidPrice.cs` | DCV004 | `Math.Round(..., 2, AwayFromZero)` in `SpreadBps` | Same reason as `Mid`: a computed value. |

For the nearest rounds of computed values (`FillStats`, `Volatility`, `Mid`, `SpreadBps`), a last-digit difference at an exact midpoint is acceptable. Nothing downstream depends on it.

I also checked for conversions the analyzer can't see. There are no boxed `Convert.ToDecimal(object)` calls, no `IConvertible.ToDecimal` calls and no JSON double-to-decimal readers. `Quote.Parse` only does `double.Parse`, which isn't affected.

The new `ToDecimal` calls throw on NaN or infinity, where the old casts and `Math.Round` didn't. The affected sites are `LotSizer`, `OrderText`, `PriceRounding`, `TickInfo`, `PnlReport`, `BalanceCheck` and `LineTotal`. All of them take written values, but `PnlReport` converts a product. I left it that way and didn't add input checks.
